dossier.architecture: Trench turret with narrow swept envelope, live-bottom singulation and deliberately low drivetrain load.

subsystems.drivetrain: 29.5×24.5-inch base; custom narrow-tread modules replaced by MK5s after defense practice exposed poor resistance to pushing.
subsystems.intake: Impact-compliant rack/gear deploy; dynamic ramp replaced by a kicker deployed once to avoid trapping fuel.
subsystems.transfer: Eleven floor rollers, independently powered vertical belts and vertical anti-jam roller feed active C-shaped uptake. Ratios iterated to control congestion.
subsystems.scoring: Compact offset ball path within turret bearing reduces outer sweep; connected back rollers target low spin. Custom narrow cable chain permits reported 640-degree travel.
subsystems.endgame: Original L3 abandoned for mass/complexity; compact threaded-rod L1 substituted.
subsystems.controls: Turret-mounted camera plus backup Limelights; velocity-compensated aiming. Worlds was first official competition of this configuration according to interview.

versions: Drive-module swap followed physical defense testing.
Multiple feed ratios and manufacturing revisions preceded Worlds; L3-to-L1 is a distinct capability reduction.
dossier.analysis: Turret rotation range is a packaging outcome. Offsetting the ball path, compact wiring and low motors reserve hopper volume and permit defense-resistant aiming; transferring only its shooter wheel dimensions would lose that system-level benefit.
limits: Only the reviewed published configurations are established; intermediate changes may be undocumented.

context_documents.title: 2026-1690 · Precondition fuel before a compact turret, then manage defended stability
context_documents.body:
# 2026-1690: Precondition fuel before a compact turret, then manage defended stability

Focused study supplement. Not a full binder/CAD review, exhaustive subsystem specification, every-version history or visual interview watch.

## Published / retained construction account

The interview describes eleven active carbon/silicone floor rollers powered by an X60 through a stated 2:1 reduction, with 3-mm-pitch GT2 inter-roller belts. A later acceleration stage is described as delivering approximately 8 m/s with near-zero incoming spin. Compact turret packaging shares shafts and places hood-drive hardware to limit diameter. A defended shooting mode cancels shooting on the move.

## Team-stated reasoning or boundary

The team explicitly cites efficiency at small pulley radii for its belt choice and compactness for the turret transmission layout. Its defended mode is explained as planting the robot to resist being pushed and emptying more accurately.

## Engineering interpretation — analyst inference

Preconditioning is a useful way to separate high-volume transport from precision release. A turret receiving fuel with controlled velocity and spin needs to add less correction, but it inherits errors in every upstream roller and transfer gap. The reported 8 m/s is an internal-stage claim, not a measured final trajectory specification or match-average rate. A planted mode also shows why turret capability does not require moving continuously: the best control mode depends on contact conditions. A future implementation must budget traction and battery demand for both upstream acceleration and chassis resistance.

## Proposed validation — not performed

Measure entrance velocity/spin distribution, current at each stage, and accuracy under controlled lateral contact. Compare planted and moving modes with the same fuel condition and load rather than ranking them from an undefended demo.

## Limits

Focused technical passages and the retained dossier are the evidence scope. Exact event installation, complete CAD tolerances and all intermediate revisions are not certified.

## Sources and navigation

- [https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=n5HWLSWU4eg](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=n5HWLSWU4eg)

source_reviews.title: Orbit 1690 KEPLER reveal and technical replies
source_reviews.review_basis: Read team-authored replies via Discourse JSON
source_reviews.facts: Covers capacity and fuel loss, L1 decision, shot calibration, moving aim under defense, electrical behavior and PTFE lining.
source_reviews.limitations: Published recovery and capacity estimates are team accounts. The thread passages do not establish every competition revision.

source_review.whole_robot_explanation: Orbit’s KEPLER combines a low trench-capable turret with a bulk-to-single fuel path. The team’s public discussion supplies specific reasons for some choices: low added inertia and lower feedback gain reduced electrical demand at the moving shooter, friction-reducing surfaces helped the singulator, and a defensive operating mode addressed the mismatch between commanded and actual motion during contact. This architecture buys freedom to aim without turning the chassis for every release. It spends that benefit on narrow-path feed development, cable travel and pose quality.
piece_flow: The prior dossier describes pickup into a live-bottom hopper. The team’s thread reports open-bin fuel loss and an approximate capacity estimate rather than an always-retained load.
Fuel converges through low-friction lined walls into a single corridor. The reduced side friction helps fuel translate as powered elements drive the stream.
The turret aims the shot. The team describes an empirical speed scale and a compression term to adapt the modeled release, with a live trim available.
source_review.packaging_and_motion: The moving turret and its wiring must clear the trench configuration across hood and yaw settings. Orbit describes changing conductor size along the circuit and limiting demand at the shooter. This is a packaging and power interaction, because the harness section that must move differs from a fixed run. Under defense, the commands and actual chassis motion can diverge. The driver can disable moving-shot compensation and command an X-wheel stance.

subsystems.name: Hopper and single-stream transfer
subsystems.construction: Live bottom in the older dossier. Team confirms polycarbonate supporting thin PTFE and PTFE on corridor side walls.
subsystems.operation: Advance fuel from the bulk store into a single launcher stream.
subsystems.team_rationale: Team identified low friction as the purpose of the lining and described losses from the open tank.
subsystems.engineering_analysis: A smooth wall reduces drag but a single exit can still bridge when several balls arrive together.
subsystems.interfaces: Collector delivery, floor motion and convergence geometry must remain compatible as fill changes.
subsystems.service_and_failure_modes: Inspect liner attachment and edge wear after impact or repeated jam reversals.
subsystems.unknowns: Roller geometry, measured rate and loaded retention.

subsystems.name: Turret and shot controls
subsystems.construction: Chassis-independent aim with a moving harness. Team describes low added inertia, empirical release compensation and controller rumble for lower voltage.
subsystems.operation: Aim while moving in normal operation, and allow a driver-selected defense stance when contact invalidates prediction.
subsystems.team_rationale: Desired velocity was less noisy than measured motion, but impact disturbances motivated a separate mode.
subsystems.engineering_analysis: Identify misses by voltage, contact state and fuel wear to separate control error from release error.
subsystems.interfaces: Shot calculation, chassis motion and drive current share the same operating budget.
subsystems.service_and_failure_modes: Check repeatability after a low-voltage burst and after motion near a wiring travel limit.
subsystems.unknowns: No recorded event-ready thresholds or transfer gating.

revisions: Team says it tested L3 and stayed with L1 because L3 did not work as desired.
Open hopper behavior, proposed net testing and trench clearance were discussed together. Net installation is not established by that post.
Team described a calibration mismatch with worn shop fuel and later changes to shot parameters.
transferable_principles: Validate moving-shot inputs during contact and across voltage, since chassis command can differ substantially from actual release-point motion.
Measure friction and singulation under packing pressure, not only with isolated balls.
Calibrate with worn and event fuel at multiple distances to separate release-scale and compression effects.
disconfirming_conditions: A narrower serial path can lose to a drum if loaded throughput is too low to capitalize on heading independence.
A command-velocity feedforward can be useful in clear space but becomes inaccurate under collisions or wheel slip.
Low added inertia only holds up if speed recovers between actual arrivals under simultaneous drive demand.
remaining_gaps: Complete turret sweep and live-bottom construction dimensions, deployed control snapshot, and independent discharge and scoring traces. Base dossier’s drivetrain revision was not independently confirmed by the reviewed posts.
recommended_images: Reveal thread post 115 for the corridor liner context. Request an overhead loaded singulation view and a side view showing hood and harness clearance.
